messages:
alice_sales: POC with Contoso hitting a blocker. Their app fails TLS to our private endpoint intermittently. They say DNS resolves to the interface endpoint IP, TCP connect succeeds but their app logs: 'x509: certificate is valid for redwood-host, not api.contoso.internal'. Customer on a security review, need quick options before their deadline.

tom_se: Ouch. Could be cert SAN mismatch or SNI rewrite. Do we have a cert that contains api.contoso.internal? If not, can they accept Host header change? Ask for curl/openssl output from the failing host.

alice_sales: They provided quick curl -v and output from their app host:
* Rebuilt connection to 10.10.20.7 (10.10.20.7) port 443
* TLS handshake completed
* SSL certificate: CN=redwood-host, SAN=redwood-host
* curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate is not valid for requested name

And dig:
; <<>> DiG 9.11.5 <<>> api.contoso.internal
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.contoso.internal. 300 IN A 10.10.20.7

They also tested from a jump host in same VPC and it works fine.

rachel_sre: If jump host works but app doesn't, likely something in the app's pod/node path is rewriting SNI or doing TLS interception. Also check whether the app uses IP-based TLS verification instead of hostname (some libs do), and whether it pins CN.

irfan_neteng: Another angle: interface endpoints backended to our NLB; if the NLB certificate CN/SAN is redwood-host but their app expects api.contoso.internal, mismatch occurs. For Private deployments we can support bringing a customer cert or map a SAN. Short term: they can use an SNI override by setting TLS SNI to api.contoso.internal when initiating, or use curl --resolve to force Host and SNI.

alice_sales: They said they can't change the application to set custom SNI or Host header easily. What's a low-friction workaround we can recommend?

tom_se: Two options:
1) On their side: put a tiny reverse-proxy (nginx) in front of the app that rewrites Host/SNI and talks to 10.10.20.7. Fast to spin up as a sidecar or small instance.
2) On our side: if they're on a Dedicated/Private plan, we can add their hostname to the cert SAN or accept a customer-provided cert on the endpoint. That requires ticket and approval but is standard for enterprise customers.

rachel_sre: Also confirm endpoint security group allows ephemeral ports back to the client and that there's no appliance (proxy/IDS) doing TLS inspection which would replace certs. Ask them to run:

openssl s_client -connect 10.10.20.7:443 -servername api.contoso.internal -showcerts

and

sudo tcpdump -nni any host 10.10.20.7 and port 443 -c 200 -w /tmp/tls.pcap

Post the s_client cert chain and we can verify who issued the cert.

alice_sales: They uploaded the s_client output (pasted):
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=redwood-host
   i:/CN=Redwood Intermediate
---
Server returned certificate chain
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 3150 bytes and written 512 bytes
---

irfan_neteng: Issuer looks like our intermediate, so the cert is coming from us (not a proxy). That means our endpoint is presenting redwood-host cert. So either their app expects a different hostname or their resolver is returning our IP but with a different expected name. Can they share the exact TLS validation error from the app stack (library and message)?

alice_sales: App stack is a Go HTTP client, error: x509: certificate is valid for redwood-host, not api.contoso.internal

tom_se: Conclusion: cert SAN mismatch. Immediate options for them:
- Use a small nginx sidecar to rewrite Host/SNI (fast, no code change)
- We can schedule a cert SAN update / customer cert on their private endpoint (requires ent. flow)
- If they can run curl with --resolve or configure OS-level hosts override, that's temporary for testing

ops-bot: Incident note created: POC-1923 cert-mismatch. Assigned to tom_se and rachel_sre.

zoom-bot: Zoom link created for triage call 1732105900

alice_sales: I'll propose the nginx sidecar as the quickest path for the demo tomorrow and open the enterprise cert request. Thanks all, I'll post the pcap and any additional errors after the call.

rachel_sre: If they send the pcap we can confirm there is no transparent TLS terminator. If everything's clean, we'll proceed with SAN/cert plan.
